source: src/eval/compare_session7.py (docs/prompt_session7.md, COMPARISONS and POWER AND THE BAR)
contamination: Known contamination: Laya's and ModernBERT's pretraining text may include PubMed pages; reader v1's own training text excluded PubMedQA's articles. Qwen3's pretraining text is not published and may include PubMed pages, PubMedQA and the UCI data, which would favor arm B. Every PQA-A and PQA-U item used in session 7 passed the 13-word check against the 1,000 PQA-L items, except that phase 3 read session 4's training records unchanged, as v0.1 did. Session 4's notes on Duan stand: PubMedQA contexts are PubMed abstracts that PubMed-trained readers may have seen with their conclusions; Duan trained on 445 PQA-L items that may overlap the official test list, and on a random 20,000-encounter UCI sample that may overlap our test split. Both favor Duan.
one_run: Each arm and each recipe ran once; retraining alone moved PubMedQA log loss by about 0.023 per run in this project (results/fiorillo_v0_2/retry_check.json), so a difference in E2 or E3, in either direction, can come partly from the run itself, and a worse result for arm B is not evidence that the base is worse in general.

1.rule: ECE at most the limit on each question (the larger of 0.05 and the 95th percentile of a calibrated model's ECE, fixed in release_candidate.json before any test prediction)

2.rule: log loss below the prior's on both questions, 95 percent interval of the difference excluding zero

3.rule: in E4, macro-F1 not below Duan's point estimate (top answer on the PubMedQA yes or no items; for readmission, decision weights fitted on the validation split as in session 4's correction 3), Duan on its own wording

4.rule: route (a) or route (b) (docs/prompt_session7.md, POWER AND THE BAR); differences are the candidate minus v0.1 in log loss, with 10,000 paired resamples

a.rule: PubMedQA's 97.5 percent interval wholly below zero, and readmission's 95 percent interval's lower end at or below zero

b.rule: readmission's 97.5 percent interval wholly below zero, and PubMedQA's 95 percent interval's lower end at or below zero
